summary: Revise at 6.6, up from 6.0. The ship bar is 7.5 and Caiman scores 7. Every gate recorded in report.json is green at draft (768x320) and at export (1536x448). The template gate is now run and passes: 1 design.set patch (/manufacturing), 967,333 bytes against the 1 MB stock budget, cold design and graph reload identical. The round fixed real things. The twig is now one 63.9 mm branch with 26 nodes. It crosses the 013 table diagonally and runs down both shank walls nearly to the palm. The Straif mark is on the palm crest, the stalk rises from the twig to the fruit, the stamen needles are gone, and the spurs on the shank have knobbly root swells. At 300 px, uncaptioned, it still reads at once as flowering blackthorn with a sloe. Three things keep it below Caiman. (1) The calyx still reads as a claw head, not a fruit's calyx. The five sepals are now rounded pods, but they stand apart from the stone on the table, evenly spaced like prongs, and with the stalk they make six. In face.png the top and right sepals still show flat sliced tops and square ends, and none of them wraps the fruit. (2) The surface execution is not clean. stones.png shows stair-stepped, sheared facets on the twig at the spur and blossom roots near the table. A torn, ragged lip runs along the full line where the twig meets the band. Flat-ended banded collar segments remain on the right shank (hero.png around x1330-1420, y880-1080; shoulder.png around x1300-1360, y640-760). The blossoms are puffy and balloon-like, with crumpled, creased hearts. The bark is lumpy and smeared rather than furrowed. (3) Density is still well under Caiman and the Reptilia signets. The twig is a single strand on one edge of each wall. The outer shank crest, the far half of each wall, the cheeks either side of the table and most of the head are bare polish, and the two twig ends stop about 9 mm short of the Straif mark (palm.png). One open item from round 1 needs an answer: the export's section diagnostic labels its thinnest clusters 'blossom: opposite wall' at 0.14-0.20 mm (for example at [11.25, -5.25, +/-0.75] and [12.75, 2.25, -0.75]). That contradicts the stated 0.84 mm petal rim, because an opposite-wall hit is a true through-section, not relief read at a slant. One concrete round can close all of this: rebuild the calyx as a cup that wraps the fruit, clean the twig joins and the seam, and add a second shoot and wall bark for density.
strengths: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption: a dark thorny branch, white-gold five-petal blossoms and a blue-black round fruit say blackthorn or sloe (hero-300, face-300, contact-300).
The theme now travels: one continuous 63.9 mm twig crosses the table diagonally and runs down both shank walls toward the palm (side.png, reverse.png, shoulder.png).
The Straif Ogham mark is on the palm crest (palm.png), and the stalk now rises from the twig to the fruit (face.png).
The silhouette is distinct: a diagonal thorned branch with spurs breaking the outline on every view, unlike the planned cane, ivy and holly rings.
The colour hierarchy holds: dark wood, bright gold blossoms, blue-black onyx.
The spurs on the shank have knobbly root swells and alternate lean, which reads as blackthorn wood (palm.png, side.png).
Gates are clean, and the template gate passes with 1 patch, under budget.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: This now passes, though only narrowly. One branch runs from the head down both walls, and the Straif mark sits on the palm. Nothing is scattered. The twig ends do stop about 9 mm short of the Straif mark, which leaves the palm crest reading as bare stock with a small mark on it.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: In hero-300 and face-300 it reads as a flowering thorny branch with a dark round fruit, which says blackthorn or sloe. The claw-like sepals are the one element that argues for 'prong-set stone'.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: stones.png shows stair-stepped, sheared facets on the twig at the spur and blossom roots (around x550-1000, y1050-1130), and a gold blocky step on the spur root at far left. A ragged, torn lip runs along the twig-to-band contact. The blossom hearts are crumpled and creased. Straif in palm.png and reverse.png renders with faint doubled or stepped outlines.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit or buds
checklist.reason: The onyx is visible, its colour is right for a sloe, and the stalk now reaches it from the twig. But the calyx reads as six evenly spaced prongs standing apart from the stone on the table, not as sepals cupping the fruit. The top and right sepals in face.png still show flat sliced tops and square ends.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: Flat-ended banded collar segments remain on the right shank (hero.png, shoulder.png). The spurs over the head are still straight machined cones. The sepal tops are sliced flat.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The 013 table edge and walls are intact (bare-vs-finished.png). The ragged table rim is present on the bare stock too.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: The diagonal branch with outward spurs over a round signet is its own outline.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large, medium and small forms are present, but the ornament is one strand covering roughly 40% of the outer surface. The cheeks, the head beyond the stone, the outer shank crest and the far half of each wall are bare polish. Caiman and the Reptilia signets are worked over the whole head and shank.

punch_list.zone: Sloe mount: 'Calyx cup' and 'Calyx sepal 1-5' at sloe centre xz (-0.3, -2.2)
punch_list.change: Make the calyx hold the fruit, not ring it. Close the gap between the sepals and the stone, so each sepal rises from the cup and lies against the stone's lower curve with no table visible between sepal and onyx. Make the sepals broad and overlapping at the base: each 1.8-2.0 mm wide, so neighbours touch or overlap by 0.2-0.4 mm at the cup and part only over their outer half. Reflex the tips 10-20 deg outward. Round over the sliced tops and square ends of every sepal with at least a 0.3 mm radius. Keep the 0.84 mm margin section.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and stones.png the sepals form one continuous gold cup under the onyx, with no polished table showing between any sepal and the stone, and no sepal shows a flat top face or square end. In hero-300 a viewer sees a fruit in its calyx, not a stone in six prongs.

punch_list.zone: Twig over the head: all spur and blossom roots, and the twig-to-band contact along its full 63.9 mm length
punch_list.change: Remove the stair-stepped and sheared facets at the roots by fairing every root into the wood with a 0.3-0.5 mm blend. Remove the remaining flat-ended banded collar segments on the right shank (nodes about 18-24). Replace the ragged lip where the twig meets the band with a clean 0.3-0.4 mm seam bead or fillet that follows the contact line. Rebuild the bark as 3-5 continuous longitudinal fissures, 0.15-0.25 mm deep, plus scattered lenticel dashes, in place of the lumpy, smeared surface.
punch_list.acceptance: At 1600 px in stones.png, hero.png and shoulder.png: no stepped or sheared facet on the wood, no flat-ended collar band on any segment, and a smooth, continuous seam where the twig meets the band. Bark fissures read as unbroken lines along the twig.

punch_list.zone: Density: the opposite edge of each shank wall, the outer shank crest from theta about +/-40 to 180 deg, both cheeks of the head, and the palm crest either side of Straif
punch_list.change: Add a second, thinner shoot (0.5-0.8 mm radius) that branches from the main twig at the shoulders and runs along the other edge of each wall, crossing the main twig once per side. Give it 3-4 small spurs (1.0-1.6 mm) and 1-2 buds or small blossoms (2.2-2.6 mm) per side. Carry both shoots to within 2 mm of the Straif mark, so the branch frames it. Add shallow wall bark (0.2-0.3 mm furrows) between the two shoots, so the walls are not bare polish.
punch_list.acceptance: In palm.png the shoots end within 2 mm of Straif on both sides. In side.png and reverse.png wood runs along both edges of both walls. No bare polished patch larger than 8 mm x 4 mm remains outside the bore, the table and the palm crest.

punch_list.zone: Blossoms (nodes 2, 5, 8, 11, 13 and the rest along the twig), and the spurs over the head (spurs 1-11)
punch_list.change: Make the blossoms crisper. Flatten each petal to a shallow cup (rise at most 0.35 mm above the rim), keep a 0.15-0.2 mm recessed gap between petals, and replace the crumpled heart with a clean domed boss ringed by 8-12 round stamen beads (0.15-0.2 mm). Give the straight cone spurs over the head the same root swell as the shank spurs, plus a 0.15-0.3 mm curve along the axis.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png each blossom shows five distinct, smooth petals and a clean round heart with no creases or folds. In face.png the spurs over the head show a root swell and a curved axis.

punch_list.change: Explain or fix the 0.14-0.20 mm opposite-wall readings on the blossoms. An opposite-wall hit is a through-section, which contradicts the stated 0.84 mm petal rim. Either show that these are petal tips overhanging the band (where the ray exits into the gap between petal and band) and thicken that gap or fuse it, or thicken the petal there to at least 0.84 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json either has no 'blossom: opposite wall' cluster under 0.8 mm, or gives each such cluster a stated cause that a cross-section through its near_mm point confirms. thinnest_wall_mm stays >= 0.8.

punch_list.zone: Straif bench-cut on the palm crest
punch_list.change: Clean the Straif outline: one crisp 0.3 mm-deep cut with no doubled or stepped edges. The stem is 6 mm and the five diagonal strokes are 1.6 x 0.35 mm each.
punch_list.acceptance: In palm.png Straif shows single, crisp edges with no doubled lines or stair-steps.
